summary: H.R. 10357, the Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act, amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to reform the tax treatment of digital assets. It establishes tax rules for digital asset transactions, creates exceptions for small fees, sets simplified accounting methods for widely traded digital assets, aligns rules for digital assets with comparable traditional financial assets, applies existing tax anti-abuse rules, clarifies mining and staking taxation, adjusts broker reporting requirements, and establishes a Digital Asset Voluntary Disclosure Program.

affected_groups.effect: Face new exemptions for small transaction fees, simplified accounting choices for widely traded assets, specific rules for stablecoins, and opportunities to resolve past tax issues via a voluntary disclosure program.
Subject to updated broker reporting rules, new mark-to-market accounting availability, and modified tax anti-harbour and anti-abuse regulations.
affected_groups.group: Digital asset brokers, dealers, and traders

affected_groups.effect: Subject to clear ordinary income treatment and specific sourcing rules for income derived from digital asset validation supporting activities.

key_provisions: Provides an exception from recognizing gain or loss on the disposition of digital assets used to pay de minimis network or transaction fees not exceeding $10.
Allows taxpayers to elect a simplified accounting method for widely traded digital assets, treating net gains and losses as short-term capital gains or losses.
Establishes tax rules for U.S. dollar stablecoin transactions, setting basis and realization criteria based on redemption value.
Extends traditional securities lending, dealer/trader mark-to-market election rules, and trading safe harbors to cover eligible digital assets.
Applies existing tax anti-abuse provisions, such as wash sale and constructive sale rules, to traded digital assets.
Clarifies that income from digital asset validation supporting activities (like mining and staking) is treated as ordinary income and outlines sourcing rules.
Establishes a Digital Asset Voluntary Disclosure Program allowing eligible taxpayers to remedy past digital asset tax violations under specific terms and reduced penalties.
missing_information: Specific details on future regulations and guidance to be issued by the Secretary of the Treasury regarding enforcement and anti-abuse provisions.
Exact revenue impacts or cost estimates associated with the tax changes.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 10357, the Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act, amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to reform the tax treatment of digital assets. It establishes tax rules for digital asset transactions, creates exceptions for small fees, sets simplified accounting methods for widely traded digital assets, aligns rules for digital assets with comparable traditional financial assets, applies existing tax anti-abuse rules, clarifies mining and staking taxation, adjusts broker reporting requirements, and establishes a Digital Asset Voluntary Disclosure Program.
summary_detail.significance: The bill comprehensively alters how federal tax law applies to digital assets, stablecoins, mining, staking, and related transactions. It affects individuals, traders, brokers, and corporations involved in the digital asset economy by creating specific compliance standards, reporting exceptions, and penalty-relief avenues.
